name: Obedience… or Oddity?
description:
Unearthed at a flea market in Southern France, this mysterious vintage action figure set—featuring an anthropomorphic dog and a kneeling human with a treat on his nose—has collectors and artists equally baffled.

No brand. No markings. No packaging.
Just two worn-out plastic figures, a dog in a red tank top, and a man kneeling with a magnetic, removable dog treat perfectly balanced on his face.

Was this a forgotten toy line from the late '70s or early '80s? A one-off satirical art piece? Or maybe something that was never meant to be sold at all?

All we know is:
It exists. It’s strange. And we kind of love it.

Would you display this in your home—or hide it in the attic forever?

name: Megaraptor namunhuaiquii
description:
*Megaraptor namunhuaiquii* was a large theropod dinosaur that lived in what is now Patagonia, Argentina, during the Late Cretaceous period, roughly 90 million years ago. It's best known for its enormous hand claws, some over 35 centimeters long, originally mistaken for foot claws similar to those of dromaeosaurs when the species was first described in 1998.

Estimated at around 8 meters long, *Megaraptor* belonged to a group called Megaraptora, whose exact placement among theropods is still debated. Some studies link them to tyrannosauroids, while others place them closer to allosauroids or as an early-diverging branch of their own.

Unlike the short arms of other large theropods, *Megaraptor* had long, powerful forelimbs built for grasping, suggesting it relied on those massive hooked claws to snag prey. Fossils come mainly from the Portezuelo Formation, offering a glimpse into the diverse predator community of Cretaceous South America.

It is the smallest of the bone-cracking hyenas, having a smaller and less specialised skull. The Body length can range from 85 to 130 cm and the tail measures 25-40 cm. I started by sculpting the model in ZBrush, beginning with a rough shape and slowly refining the details. Once I was happy with the sculpt, I retopologized it to make the model cleaner and easier to work with. Then, I created the UVs so I could paint the textures properly without any stretching or distortion. For the texturing, I hand-painted everything using my own 2D art style. I wanted it to have a unique, hand drawn look. At the end I set up a simple rig to give it an Idle animation. It was a fun challenge to bring my painting style into 3D, and I learned a lot in the process. Seeing it all come together was really exciting, and I’m so proud of the final result!

Edit! I returned to this project a few months later to update the textures, re render and I'm very happy with how it turn out!

John McCormick from Occidential College provided funding and guidance. name: American Cockroach - insect
description: The American cockroach (Periplaneta americana) is among the largest and most resilient cockroach species. Despite its name, it originated in Africa and spread globally. It thrives in warm, humid environments and is commonly found in basements, sewers, and kitchens. Growing up to 53mm, it has a reddish-brown exoskeleton, long antennae, and fully developed wings, though it rarely flies. It is an omnivorous scavenger, feeding on decaying organic matter, starches, and even non-food items like paper. Highly adaptable, it can survive weeks without food and endure harsh conditions. Cockroaches play a role in decomposition but are also vectors for bacteria like Salmonella and allergens that can trigger asthma. Their rapid reproduction and resilience make them difficult pests to control. Despite their reputation, cockroaches are evolutionary marvels, existing for over 300 million years. Studying them has led to insights in robotics and medicine, proving their importance beyond their pest status.
